title: Mixed Signs
logline: At first light a fishing crew stands between a sea that looks calm and a forecast that says otherwise, with the boat half-ready and the conversation going round again.
human_question: How do you decide when the signs will not agree?

situation.what_happens: At the turn of a season a crew has to decide each morning whether to put out. They read the sky, the swell and the wind, and they also read forecasts on phones and radios that do not always agree with what they can see, or with each other. Staying ashore costs a day's income; going out in the wrong weather can cost far more. The boat is made half ready while the decision is still open, and then it is either pushed out or left.
situation.who_is_involved: A crew who share the risk and the catch; the owner of the boat, who may not be aboard; the families whose week depends on the day; and the buyers waiting on the shore.
situation.what_is_at_stake: Income, gear and lives. Also standing: a skipper who stays ashore too often, or who goes out once too many times, is judged by everyone watching.
situation.how_it_unfolds: It begins before light with the reading of the sea, stays open while the signs contradict one another, and closes when the light or the tide decides for them. It ends at sea, or ashore with the nets from the last rough night to untangle. Reality decides both the weather and whether anyone turns out to have been right.

concept_merge.why_together: C008 describes a mind that cannot come to a decision about its object, felt as flat rather than painful [C008-P:L34; C008-P:L30], and the digest is careful that honest uncertainty about something not yet knowable is a different thing [C008-P:L36]. C074 adds the knot, which ties today to tomorrow and is undone by patient work rather than force. A morning in which money and risk hang on signs that will not agree holds both: an unsettled decision, and the slow work that fills the waiting.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That hesitation in front of genuinely mixed evidence is not the state the sources warn about, and may be the most skilful thing available. Put together, the two concepts mark a boundary that most talk about doubt erases.

concept_links.why: The digest gives the general description of doubt as an inability to decide about the object [C008-P:L34] and in the same breath separates it from honest not-knowing of what one cannot yet investigate, which the sources say may not be unwholesome at all [C008-P:L36]. This idea exists mainly to hold that boundary: a crew weighing a doubtful forecast is not deluded, and a film may never say they are.

Among the compendium's images is the knot that ties the present to what follows and takes patient work to undo. If the crew stays ashore, the tangled nets from the last rough night are the day's real work, and the image is left where it lies.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: The texts separate the doubt they warn about from ordinary not-knowing. Standing still in front of signs that genuinely disagree can be the wise thing, not the confused one.
what_must_be_real: The crew, the weather and the decision. No decision is prompted, delayed or reversed for the camera, and no one goes to sea because a film is being made.
position_hint: middle, if ever used on its own: it belongs wherever a group needs to mark the difference between confusion and a considered refusal to decide.
risks: Presenting hesitation as a flaw when it is often wisdom.
Danger to the crew and to anyone filming at sea.
Net-mending as documentary cliché with no real person at its centre.
A working crew reduced to an illustration of a mental state.
drop_if: The weather simply decides for everyone, leaving no open decision.

connections.note: Its costly-decision strand and its guard on honest not-knowing now live inside the opening film.
Knots in nets and ropes on stakes: two images of being tied that belong to people's real work.

selection.reason: Folded into IDEA-0054, which gains its costly-decision strand and its guard separating honest not-knowing from the doubt the sources warn about.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
